findings.detail: Validated synthetic level 1,000,000 / XP 100,000,000 saves paid 50,000 at memory_archive and 12,000,070 at starlibrary.study for 0 admitted XP while old UI claimed the nominal million/credited XP. Current preview, confirmation and result name 0 or the partial amount and retain the same price, permission and assets.

At level 100 / XP 1017 / unspent talent points 2,000,000, memory_archive and exchange advance to level 101; starlibrary advances to level 102. Existing point count remains capped, but baseline logs claimed +2 for each upgrade. Current logs disclose +0 and the two uncredited points. Boundary +1 and +2 receipts also pass.

XP entrance inventory is combat kills, exchange salvage, memory_archive accept and starlibrary study. XP math and HP, gold, item, RNG and unknown-field behavior match the input version. Combat overflow now has a bounded saved log; opening the resulting chest does not credit XP again.

findings.detail: Unconfirmed and repeated choices cannot charge; insufficient registered cost refuses unchanged; leave preserves assets. Injected primary write failure and stale full expected snapshot retain exact originals; mirror failure retains a valid committed primary and returns a visible warning. findings.kind: P3 remains an opportunity, no new numerical bug demonstrated
findings.detail: Eight fixed-policy journeys per version compare two priority builds, two spending policies and depths 200/400. All result rows, combat traces and complete final-state fingerprints after the existing runId normalization match exactly. No death in these fixed policies does not justify a balance patch or a human win-rate conclusion.

excludedFalsePositives: The character level cap is distinct from the saved XP cap: a max-level character with empty XP still accepts a million XP into its balance under existing rules.
Large already-stored imported XP can level a character up even when the new receipt is 0. This is consumption of prior XP, not a negative or newly admitted reward.
The real receipt equals the XP counter change plus the independent arithmetic cost of all actual upgrades; a negative counter difference is not a negative reward.
The task keeps existing voluntary zero-credit payment/exchange permissions. Explicit capacity disclosure is the fix, not a silent new ban or refund policy.
An event price already in a valid V5 snapshot remains authoritative, including 0 and 100,000,000. The review does not recalculate it from current level.
Raw finalStateSha256 from the preserved deep script uses its explicit runId normalization. No log/XP field was deleted to force equality this round.

developmentFailures.classification: reviewer QA harness API-shape error, not product failure
developmentFailures.cause: First draft compared loadSave(storage) itself with a game state, overlooking its stable {state,recovered,warning} result envelope.
developmentFailures.fix: Changed the assertion to loadSave(storage).state; preserved the complete original failure report. Reran the baseline and candidate with all six fault cases passing. No production code or original test assertion was changed for this correction.

scopeLimits: Synthetic extreme saves do not measure how often a player reaches caps.
Ephemeral option.experience is checked against independent arithmetic; it is never saved as a new state field.
Non-narrative A/B equality excludes only log and event.outcome. Those two text surfaces are separately checked for accepted amounts, point caps and unchanged validator length limits.
No browser, hardware, storage-quota, physical-power-loss or multiplayer concurrency claim is made.
A mirror write failure occurs after the authoritative primary commit and is reported as a recoverable condition, never as a rollback.
Fixed automated policies; not human play, population win rates or evidence of optimal choices.
The audit normalizes runId to the literal normalized before hashing each complete final state. Matching that fingerprint is not an assertion that separately generated run IDs are equal.
Whole-run spending policies consume different actual dice. Differences between two policies cannot identify an isolated causal benefit of a single purchase.
Talent priority policies eventually learn many shared finite nodes; their labels are not mutually exclusive character classes.
The current rows do not include balanced-policy forge/respec counterfactual examples; their absence is not evidence that those options have no value.
Gross paid and net spending are different columns and are not added together.
No timing speedup or hardware performance conclusion is drawn from script durations.
remainingBrowserCheckSentToRoot: The newly shared experience preview also enters exchange confirmations; verify the 64-character item-name / dual-zero confirmation at 1366x768 because that is a touched layout. This is a targeted coverage request, not an asserted bug.
